problem: Existing AudioGoal agents must learn basic wayfinding and audio-visual understanding from limited samples, and they perceive only forward (90-degree FoV) even though waypoint-level decisions are effectively omnidirectional, giving incomplete maps and direction-biased waypoint predictions.
motivation: Basic wayfinding skills such as moving to a short-term target, avoiding collisions and passing doors are shared across navigation tasks, and PointGoal agents are near-perfect thanks to large-scale training. Humans also turn toward a sound before deciding. Reusing PointGoal knowledge and gathering panoramic observations should make the agent more sample-efficient and robust.
key_idea: Distill a well-trained PointGoal policy into a waypoint-based AudioGoal policy using only its most confident steps (CCPD), and average waypoint maps from four rotated observations at inference (OIG).
insight: Naive distillation over all steps hurts (SR 50.0 vs 53.1 baseline), while entropy-based confidence selection/weighting gives SR 59.5, so the teacher only helps where it is confident despite the task domain gap. Using the PointGoal agent directly with pseudo-GPS fails (SR 17.2), confirming the gap. OIG adds a training-free gain in SPL (45.1 to 50.8), and it also lifts the ensemble (SPL 50.0 to 62.6). Its cost is extra perception actions that are excluded from the metrics.
method: Waypoint-based base architecture (from AV-WaN): builds a top-down geometry map and acoustic map from depth and binaural audio; a GRU policy outputs an m×m waypoint score map; the agent plans with Dijkstra and executes low-level actions.

CCPD distillation: a PointGoal policy (DD-PPO init, action layer replaced and finetuned to output the action map) is queried with the same goal as the teacher; the AudioGoal student is trained with KL divergence on trajectories sampled by the student (student forcing).

Confidence-aware reweighting: teacher confidence c_P = 1/entropy of the teacher's action distribution; only the top-k (k=30) most confident steps per trajectory contribute, weighted by c_P (L_CD, loss weight 0.3), combined with PPO.

OIG: at each decision step the agent collects observations at 0/90/180/270 degrees, runs the policy on each, rotates the action maps back to a common frame and averages them; the next waypoint is sampled from the averaged map. No finetuning is needed.
Stop policy model: an additional model helps judge when to stop at the target.
Model ensemble: action maps from several models of different architectures and training strategies, chosen by grid search, are averaged; used for the SoundSpaces Challenge 2022 entry.

setting.backbone: GRU waypoint-predictor policy trained with PPO plus CCPD distillation from a DD-PPO PointGoal teacher (trained, not LLM-based)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces AudioGoal training scenes (Replica 9, Matterport3D 73); teacher is DD-PPO PointGoal pre-trained on large-scale PointGoal data, finetuned on the training split; spectrogram augmentation for the unheard split
setting.observation: egocentric depth (RGB not emphasized) plus binaural audio spectrograms, accumulated into top-down geometry and acoustic maps; 4-direction panoramic gathering at inference
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints on an m×m local map, executed with low-level actions via Dijkstra shortest-path planning
setting.privileged: none at test time (the PointGoal teacher uses GT target coordinates via GPS+compass during training only)

numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Comparisons on Soundspaces dataset), Matterport3D Unheard

numbers_note: Benchmark is the SoundSpaces AudioGoal challenge (not in the canonical list, so mapped to 'SoundSpaces'). Table 1 splits are heard/unheard rather than the standard split names. Ablation numbers on Matterport3D unheard (baseline SR 53.1, SPL 38.6; CCPD only SR 59.5, SPL 45.1) are omitted.
results: On Matterport3D unheard, ORAN reaches SR 59.4 and SPL 50.8, beating AV-WaN (SR 56.7, SPL 40.9), and on Replica unheard SPL 46.7 versus AV-WaN's 34.7. It is comparable to AV-WaN on the heard setting. The model ensemble with OIG reaches SPL 62.6 and SR 77.7, winning the SoundSpaces Challenge 2022.
limitations: OIG needs extra perception (rotation) actions per decision step, which are not counted in the metrics, so real cost is higher.
No gain over AV-WaN on the heard setting, and the method depends on a strong PointGoal teacher and on hyperparameters such as k.
